14 · Where are the meninges? A gene-based answer from the Xenium EAE atlas¶

Our images (nuclei, Pu.1, Iba1) cannot separate meninges from subpial lesion (notebook 13). The RRMAP2 Xenium 5k atlas of EAE spinal cord can: 157 sections, CFA controls and every EAE phase, 5,000 genes and the raw transcripts. Two gene layers mark the border:

  • meningeal fibroblast genes – Slc47a1, Foxc2, Crabp2, Osr1, Slc13a4, Smoc2, Wnt6, Klf5, Fmod, Cdh1: chosen from the atlas as the genes detected in meningeal fibroblasts but rarely in any other cell (table below); Ptgds and the collagens are not specific here (Ptgds spreads into many cells; collagens are shared with the lesion fibroblasts);
  • glia limitans genes – Aqp4 and Gfap: the astrocyte endfeet on the parenchymal side of the pia.

Method (lesionseg/xenium_meninges.py; scripts/xenium_transcript_rasters.py on the remote; scripts/xenium_meninges.py):

  1. All transcripts of a capture region binned at 5 µm. Tissue = transcript density above half the section's median (the edge at half maximum; a looser mask sat 15–20 µm outside the cells). Depth = distance to the tissue edge – the same definition the image pipeline uses on its own tissue mask.

  2. Every tissue pixel is assigned to its nearest edge point; edge points are grouped into 50 µm stretches.

  3. Per stretch, 5 µm depth rings (3 pooled), the pia placed two ways with opposite biases:

    • balance – the run of rings from the surface where the meningeal share of transcripts beats the glia-limitans share (each scaled between the section's surface and deep levels) and is ≥ 10 % of the way to its surface level. Immune transcripts dilute the meningeal share in swollen meninges → leans "subpial".
    • glia – the run of rings from the surface where the glia-limitans density is below half its deep level (no astrocyte endfeet yet). Astrocyte loss in lesions → leans "meningeal".

    Stretches that never reach parenchyma (flaps, tears, oblique cuts) get no pia and are left out, as are false edges: tissue whose nearest outside pixel lies in a patch with no transcripts at all (a missing field of view – a real edge always has a halo of diffused transcripts). A stretch whose pia is at 0 µm has no resolved meningeal layer – mostly meninges thinner than one 5 µm ring (a single cell), sometimes stripped. A third view, present, asks the clean question only on stretches that do have a layer: where meninges exist, which side of them is the infiltrate on?

  4. Atlas cells (curated cell types) are placed above (meninges) or below (parenchyma) the pia of their stretch.

Unit for comparisons: the section. Atlas cells ≠ our cells – the depth scales of the two datasets are not calibrated against each other (both measure from a tissue edge, but from different masks).

Gene layers against depth (all sections of a phase pooled; per 1000 transcripts)¶

The meningeal genes peak in the outer 5–15 µm; the glia limitans dips there and rises from ~20–30 µm; immune transcripts in EAE are highest at 15–40 µm – right where the two layers meet.

Are immune cells near the surface meningeal or subpial?¶

Share of atlas cells above the pia of their stretch, by depth; solid = balance, dashed = glia; middle panel = only stretches that have a meningeal layer (present). Meningeal fibroblasts are the method's control: ~87 % of them at 0–10 µm land above the pia (5 µm rings and cell positions set a floor of ~13 % misplacement).

Sensitivity: the balance definition's minimum meningeal level¶

The fibroblast control hardly moves with the threshold, so it cannot pick it; the immune shares at 0–20 µm do move (the default is 0.1). The conclusion below 20–30 µm does not depend on it.

Zoomed examples at the surface (300 µm windows)¶

Background: gene layers as above (dimmed). White line = pia (balance), yellow dashed = pia (glia), grey = tissue edge. Every atlas cell is a dot: green meningeal fibroblast, blue immune (myeloid, T, B, DC – not microglia), orange astrocyte, pink microglia, grey other. Filled = above the pia (meninges), hollow = below (parenchyma); small grey × = outside the tissue mask or on a stretch without a pia. Windows are centred on a 50 µm surface stretch picked by the criterion in the title – four per kind, from different sections.

In [9]:
cdepth = pd.read_parquet(WORK / "cells_depth.parquet").merge(pia[["section", "seg", "pia_depth_um"]], on=["section", "seg"], how="left")
cdepth["above"] = cdepth.depth <= cdepth.pia_depth_um
KIND = [(cdepth.Anno_L2.isin(X.MENINGEAL_FB), "#1baf7a", "meningeal FB"),
        (cdepth.Anno_L1_curated.isin(X.IMMUNE_L1), "#3987e5", "immune"),
        (cdepth.Anno_L1_curated == "Astrocyte", "#eda100", "astrocyte"),
        (cdepth.Anno_L2 == "Microglia", "#e87ba4", "microglia")]
cdepth["col"] = np.select([k[0] for k in KIND], [k[1] for k in KIND], "#898781")
_views = {}

def view(s):
    if s not in _views:
        r = sh[sh.section == s].iloc[0]
        c = cells_atlas[cells_atlas.section == s]
        rgb, men, tis, ext = X.section_view("outputs/xenium_rasters", r, c, pia)
        _views[s] = (r, rgb, men, X.section_view("outputs/xenium_rasters", r, c, pia, col="pia_glia_um")[1], tis, ext)
    return _views[s]

def zoom(ax, s, seg, size=300, note=""):
    r, rgb, men, men_g, tis, ext = view(s)
    cx, cy = (seg % 100000 + 0.5) * X.SEG_UM, (seg // 100000 + 0.5) * X.SEG_UM
    ax.imshow(np.clip(rgb * 0.55, 0, 1), extent=ext)
    ax.contour(men, levels=[0.5], colors="white", linewidths=1.4, extent=ext, origin="upper")
    ax.contour(men_g, levels=[0.5], colors="#eda100", linewidths=1, linestyles="--", extent=ext, origin="upper")
    ax.contour(tis, levels=[0.5], colors="#898781", linewidths=0.8, extent=ext, origin="upper")
    d = cdepth[(cdepth.section == s) & cdepth.x_centroid.between(cx - size / 2, cx + size / 2)
               & cdepth.y_centroid.between(cy - size / 2, cy + size / 2)]
    out_ = d.depth.isna() | d.pia_depth_um.isna()
    ax.scatter(d.x_centroid[out_], d.y_centroid[out_], s=10, marker="x", c="#52514e", lw=0.6)
    d = d[~out_]
    up = d.above.astype(bool)
    ax.scatter(d.x_centroid[up], d.y_centroid[up], s=16, c=d.col[up], lw=0)
    ax.scatter(d.x_centroid[~up], d.y_centroid[~up], s=16, facecolors="none", edgecolors=d.col[~up], lw=0.9)
    ax.set_xlim(cx - size / 2, cx + size / 2); ax.set_ylim(cy + size / 2, cy - size / 2)
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
    p = pia[(pia.section == s) & (pia.seg == seg)].iloc[0]
    imm = d[d.col == "#3987e5"]
    ax.set_title(f"{s} · {r.animal} · {r.group}\npia {p.pia_depth_um:.0f} µm (glia {p.pia_glia_um:.0f}) · immune above/below: "
                 f"{int(imm.above.fillna(False).sum())}/{int((~imm.above.fillna(False).astype(bool)).sum())} {note}",
                 loc="left", fontsize=8.5)

def gallery(picks, ncol=4):
    picks = list(picks)
    nrow = int(np.ceil(len(picks) / ncol))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrow, ncol, figsize=(5.2 * ncol, 5.6 * nrow), squeeze=False)
    for ax, (s, seg) in zip(axes.ravel(), picks):
        zoom(ax, s, seg)
    for ax in axes.ravel()[len(picks):]:
        ax.axis("off")
    from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
    h = [Line2D([], [], marker="o", ls="", color=c, label=l) for _, c, l in KIND] + [
        Line2D([], [], marker="o", ls="", color="#898781", label="other"),
        Line2D([], [], marker="o", ls="", mfc="none", mec="#52514e", label="hollow = below the pia"),
        Line2D([], [], color="white", lw=2, label="pia (balance)"), Line2D([], [], color="#eda100", ls="--", label="pia (glia)")]
    fig.legend(handles=h, loc="lower center", ncol=8, fontsize=9, frameon=False, facecolor="#52514e")
    plt.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.03, 1, 1)); plt.show()

def pick(df, n=4, seed=None, by=None):
    df = df.sample(frac=1, random_state=seed) if seed is not None else df.sort_values(by, ascending=False)
    return list(df.drop_duplicates("section").head(n)[["section", "seg"]].itertuples(index=False, name=None))
pia["imm_above_dens"] = pia.immune_above_pia / pia.total
pia["imm_below_dens"] = pia.immune_below_pia_0_50 / pia.total

What it means for our rule¶

Our rule calls the outer 10 µm meninges and extends the meninges into compact infiltrate connected to it, down to 80 µm. Below: how deep our rule's Pu.1⁺ meninges cells are, and – applying the Xenium share of immune cells above the pia in the same animal – how many of them would be subpial. present (stretches with a layer) is the lower bound, balance / glia over all stretches the upper.

Assumption to confirm: our animals OS1_2, P2_3, P3_1, R1_2 and R1_3 are the RRMAP2 animals RR_OS1_2, RR_P2_3, RR_P3_1, RR_R1_2 and RR_R1_3 (same names, same C/T/L levels). CFA_L2 has no match and uses the pooled CFA controls. Xenium sections of an animal are pooled over levels (few immune cells per bin otherwise); bins with < 20 Xenium immune cells fall back to the animal's phase.

In [16]:
rows = []
for r in runs:
    m = r.cells[(r.cells.section_id > 0) & (r.cells.surface_tier.astype(str) == "meninges") & r.cells.pu1_pos]
    m = m.assign(animal=m.section_name.astype(str).str.rsplit("_", n=1).str[0],
                 depth_bin=pd.cut(m.depth_um, [0, 10, 20, 30, 50, 80, 150], labels=BINS, include_lowest=True).astype(str))
    rows.append(m.groupby(["animal", "depth_bin"]).size().rename("pu1_meninges_cells").reset_index())
ours_t = pd.concat(rows).groupby(["animal", "depth_bin"], as_index=False).pu1_meninges_cells.sum()
ours_t = ours_t[ours_t.depth_bin.isin(BINS)]
grp_of = sh.drop_duplicates("animal").set_index("animal").group
phase_rate = (pd.read_csv(OUT / "above_pia_by_depth.csv").query("cell_class == 'immune'")
              .set_index(["definition", "group", "depth_bin"]).above_pia)
est = []
for dfn in ("present", "balance", "glia"):
    a = aba[(aba.definition == dfn)].set_index(["animal", "depth_bin"])
    t = ours_t.copy()
    t["xenium_animal"] = t.animal.map(TWIN)
    t["grp"] = t.xenium_animal.map(grp_of).fillna("CFA control")

    def rate(row):
        k = (row.xenium_animal, row.depth_bin)
        if isinstance(row.xenium_animal, str) and k in a.index and a.loc[k, "cells"] >= 20:
            return a.loc[k, "above_pia"]
        return phase_rate.get((dfn, row.grp, row.depth_bin), np.nan)
    t["xenium_above"] = t.apply(rate, axis=1)
    t["expected_subpial"] = t.pu1_meninges_cells * (1 - t.xenium_above)
    est.append(t.assign(definition=dfn))
est = pd.concat(est)
tab = est.pivot_table(index="depth_bin", columns="definition", values="expected_subpial", aggfunc="sum").reindex(BINS)
tab.insert(0, "pu1_meninges_cells", est[est.definition == "balance"].groupby("depth_bin").pu1_meninges_cells.sum())
display(tab.round(0))
tot = tab.pu1_meninges_cells.sum()
for dfn in ("present", "balance", "glia"):

          f"({100 * tab[dfn].sum() / tot:.0f} %); deeper than 20 µm: {tab.loc[BINS[2:], dfn].sum():,.0f} "
          f"of {tab.loc[BINS[2:], 'pu1_meninges_cells'].sum():,.0f}")

Reading¶

  • The meninges are thin. In ~40–55 % of EAE surface stretches and ~70 % in CFA controls no meningeal layer is resolved at 5 µm (a single-cell pia–arachnoid, sometimes stripped). Where there is one, it is 5–30 µm deep and thicker where the surface is infiltrated.
  • Where meninges exist, the outer 10 µm is meningeal and deeper infiltrate is subpial. On stretches with a meningeal layer, immune cells in EAE are ~89 % above the pia at 0–10 µm, ~47 % at 10–20 µm, ~20 % at 20–30 µm, ~9 % at 30–50 µm and ~4 % at 50–80 µm. Over all stretches (counting edges without a layer as subpial) the shares are lower, but every definition agrees beyond ~20 µm: most immune cells there are below the pia.
  • For our rule: the outer ≤ 10 µm layer is fine where meninges exist; the extension of the meninges into compact infiltrate down to 80 µm takes in mostly subpial lesion. A cap at ~20 µm would match the genes. Expected subpial share of our rule's Pu.1⁺ meninges cells: ~39 % (present, lower bound) to ~57–68 % (all stretches) overall, but ~78–89 % of those deeper than 20 µm (1,630–1,860 of 2,090 cells).
  • The truly ambiguous case is a dense immune band at the surface with no glia limitans and only faint fibroblast genes (see the subpial gallery): balance puts the pia at the edge, glia 25–30 µm deep. That is what the six core_at_surface annotation boxes are for.
  • It explains notebook 13: meninges and lesion interleave at 10–30 µm, so a model trained on "outer ≤ 10 µm = meninges" learns infiltrate, and no image feature separates them.
  • Which pia to trust: by the fibroblast control, balance (≈ 87 % of meningeal fibroblasts at 0–10 µm above its pia) beats glia (60–75 % in EAE, ~40 % in controls); glia is the bracket with the opposite bias.
  • Caveats. Different cells, segmentation and tissue mask than our images: the depth scales are not calibrated (treat µm values as ±5–10 µm). The pia is resolved in 5 µm rings. ~30 % of stretches (tears, flaps, oblique cuts) have none; false edges at missing fields of view are removed, but low-density patches inside sections still count as edge. The Xenium sections of "our" animals are probably not the same sections (assumption above).
